messages.subject: Object from string names using get() and eval()
messages.subject_clean: Object from string names using get() and eval()
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Quick programming question here. I'm trying to populate a set of
matrices  where the matrix (object) names are held in a list. I can
use the get() to return the object with the given name, but I'm
running into function problems when I use get() to define the matrix
object I'm trying to populate.

#Some code follows:

#Create list of matrix names:
 list.names <- c("m.1")

#Create matrix object
m.1 <- matrix(nrow=2,ncol=2)

#Return matrix m.1 from the list.names using get(). Works great!
get(list.names[1])

#Populate m.1] with some values. Doesn't work.
get(list.names[1]) <- c(1,2,3,4)

#End code

So in the last line of code, I'm getting an error:

could not find function "get<-"

Similarly, I can call m.1 using:

 eval(as.name <http://as.name>(list.name <http://list.name>[1]))

But R returns a similar 'could not find function' error.

Could someone explain the error in my approach, here?

Thanks,

-s

messages.body_plain:
Hi Scott,

Would it work (with what you're trying to do) if you populate the matrix with the values when you create it?

#Create list of matrix names:
 list.names <- c("m.1")

#Create matrix object

m.1 <- matrix(c(1,2,3,4), nrow=2,ncol=2)

get(list.names[1])

eval(as.name <http://as.name>(list.names[1])) # changed from list.name <http://list.name> to list.names

Is this what you're looking to do?

Hope this helped,
Patrick

messages.body_plain:
Hi Patrick,

Thanks for the reply!

In this example your suggestion would work, but would not work more
generally. The example I gave is simplified; in my real code there is
a subroutine that that populates the matrix from about 200 model
output files. The code uses nested for() loops to traverse the various
input and output datasets,  but showing those are not necessary to get
at the heart of the matter here.

Thanks!

-s

messages.subject: D-RUG this week: MCMC
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

We'll have our last D-RUG work session of the quarter this Wednesday.  David Harris will be giving a presentation about Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods.  From Dave:

> "I'll be talking about using Monte Carlo methods to learn about statistical models and probability distributions, especially Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC).  The presentation will mainly be aimed at beginners that have heard of MCMC but aren't entirely sure what it does or how it works."

Soon I'll send out a new survey for meeting times for the spring quarter.  See you 3-5PM Wednesday in Wickson 2124.

Noam
